key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection to reduce weld defects, thermal gradients and axial-force fluctuations in HDPE joining.
method: Develop a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model of temperature, force, material flow and defect formation.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force histories.
Use simulations and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good agreement with CEL predictions, ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99, and a peak plunge-force reduction from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N with 60 °C preheating.
watch_item: Predictive performance is demonstrated within the tested parameter space; extrapolation to other welding conditions requires further validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
